# What Is Connected TV Advertising? Should You Buy It?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-connected-tv-advertising/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-06-30 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Distribution

> Summary: Connected TV is television watched through an internet connection, with advertising bought and measured like digital media. The IAB forecast US CTV spend growing 13.8% in 2026, and CTV was about 40% of programmatic spend in the ANA's Q4 2025 benchmark. It is best entered programmatically, measured by lift rather than clicks, and worth buying once a company has a working acquisition motion, a measurable brand constraint and confirmation its category is permitted.

Connected TV (CTV) is television watched through an internet connection: streaming services, smart TV apps and devices plugged into a screen. Advertising on it is bought and measured like digital media, with audiences, frequency caps and reporting, while being seen like television, on a large screen with sound on. It is growing quickly: the IAB's 2026 Outlook forecast US CTV ad spend up 13.8%. It is best entered programmatically, measured by lift rather than clicks, and worth buying once a company has a working acquisition motion, a measurable brand constraint and confirmation that its category is permitted.

It has grown quickly because audiences moved, and because it lets companies that could never afford broadcast television buy the screen in small amounts. The IAB's January 2026 Outlook Study, based on about 200 US buyers, forecast CTV spend growing 13.8% in 2026, behind only social media. Its May 2026 digital video report put CTV growth at 11% and total US digital video spend above $80 billion, more than 60% of all TV and video ad spend for the first time.

## How it is bought

| Route | How it works | Suits | Watch for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct from a streaming service or broadcaster | Insertion order with the service's ad sales team | Large budgets wanting specific programmes | Minimum spends; one service only |
| Platform self-serve or managed | The streaming platform's own buying tools | Small tests on one platform | Category policies applied by the platform |
| Programmatic through a DSP | CTV inventory across many apps and services, with the same audience, verification and optimisation tools used for display and video | Most mid-sized buyers | Inventory transparency and fraud on open routes |

Programmatic is where most mid-sized buyers end up, because it allows small tests, audience definitions the buyer controls, and inventory across services rather than a commitment to one. The market has largely moved to curated deals. In the ANA's fourth-quarter 2025 programmatic benchmark, built with TAG TrustNet and Fiducia, CTV was about 40% of total programmatic spend and private marketplaces accounted for 100% of CTV transactions.

Curated does not mean transparent. The IAB's 2026 Digital Video Ad Spend and Strategy report, a survey of 360 US buyers, found that even on the routes buyers trust most (publisher-direct deals, programmatic guaranteed and publisher self-service) 43% had only some or no confidence in where their ads ran. On the open exchange only 33% had high confidence, and 56% of those who mistrusted it cited fraud. Our [guide to programmatic](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-programmatic-advertising/) covers the supply chain standards that help a buyer check who is selling.

## How it is measured

Impressions and completed views are the basic units. CTV ads are usually unskippable, so completion rates are high and say little. Viewability is harder than on the web: the ANA's benchmark noted that server-side ad insertion and limited signals led to more CTV impressions being classed as non-viewable, because the measurement could not confirm them, not necessarily because nobody watched.

More useful measures connect exposure to behaviour:

| Measure | What it shows | Weakness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Household visits and conversions | Whether households that saw the ad later visited or bought, matched through IP address or device graphs | Matching degrades as IP signals weaken; correlation, not cause |
| Branded search and direct traffic lift | Whether people looked for the company during flights | Noisy at small budgets |
| Geographic incrementality test | Whether outcomes rose in matched regions where ads ran versus where they did not | Needs enough budget and regions to read |

Attribution is weaker than on click-based channels because nobody clicks a television. The IAB found 39% of buyers named the lack of a direct click-through as a barrier to lower-funnel CTV, and 38% the need for a second device. The honest measurement question is whether outcomes rose where the ads ran compared with where they did not. Our pieces on [attribution versus incrementality](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/) and [campaign testing that reaches a decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/) set out how to design a geographic test that produces a decision rather than a debate.

> CTV amplifies a working acquisition motion. It does not create one.

## What it costs

Meaningfully more per thousand impressions than display or social video, reflecting the screen, the attention and the completion. Minimum tests that produce a readable signal are larger than for other channels, because the effect is measured at the household and geography level rather than per click. The IAB found small and mid-size buyers were more likely than large ones to report high cost-per-acquisition concerns, 44% against 28%, which is what that minimum looks like from a smaller budget.

## When it makes sense, and when it does not

| Buy CTV when | Do not buy it yet when |
| --- | --- |
| The product can be understood in fifteen or thirty seconds | The company has not found a channel that produces customers at a survivable cost |
| The company knows its cost per outcome on other channels and wants reach beyond them | The budget cannot support a test large enough to read |
| Brand recognition is a measured constraint: visitors convert poorly because they have never heard of the company | The category is restricted on the streaming platforms in the target geographies |
| The audience can be defined and matched, so the buy is not paying for households that could never be customers | The only measure available is completed views |

The third row on the left deserves a number before it is used as a reason. Our piece on [measuring brand in B2B](https://lowob.com/research/measuring-brand-in-b2b/) covers share of search and shortlist rate, two ways to show that recognition, not interest, is what is holding conversion back.

## For restricted categories specifically

Streaming services apply their own category policies, often stricter than the open web, and programmatic CTV inventory varies widely in what it will carry. Roku's self-serve Ads Manager is a useful example of the pattern. It requires prior approval for any cryptocurrency ad and limits approvals to items such as licensed exchanges and mining hardware in the US; it bans ads for individual securities; it requires credit, loan and insurance advertisers to show licensing on request; and it prohibits healthcare and pharmaceutical ads through the self-serve platform. Direct and programmatic deals with the same platform can carry different rules.

Before planning any CTV spend, confirm which services and exchanges will run the category, with what disclaimers, in which geographies. Where it is open, CTV can be a thinly bid channel for reviewed categories, for the usual reason: the competitors who would crowd it are in the same review queue. Our piece on [thin bidding](https://lowob.com/research/thin-bidding/) explains why that matters.

## lowob takeaways

- **CTV is TV bought like digital.** Programmatic access makes it available to mid-sized budgets.
- **Curated is not the same as transparent.** Ask where the ads ran, even on private marketplace deals.
- **Measure lift, not clicks or completions.** Geographic tests answer the only question that matters.
- **It amplifies; it does not create.** Find a working channel first.
- **Check category rules first.** Streaming platforms often restrict finance, crypto and health.

## Next move

Before any CTV spend, write down your current cost per outcome on your best channel and the lift a CTV test would need to show to beat it. Then confirm in writing which streaming services and exchanges will carry your category in your target markets.
